subject.title: Telegram: per-chat lane serialization (isolated ingress) starves messages.queue.collect — same-chat bursts never coalesce

question: Should Telegram preserve per-chat drain serialization and document same-chat collect as unsupported, or should busy same-lane spooled updates be admitted into the active followup/collect queue?
rationale: Both choices affect user-visible ordering and Telegram reliability invariants; the scoped Telegram guide requires preserving durable-before-ack, replay, lane ordering, and control-lane behavior, which automation cannot choose as a product contract.

options.title: Bridge busy lanes into collect
options.body: Implement a Telegram-aware admission path that lets later same-lane ordinary updates reach active followup/collect while preserving control lanes, ack durability, and replay safety.

options.title: Document the limitation
options.body: Keep current lane serialization and update docs/help so Telegram users are not promised same-chat collect behavior the transport path cannot currently provide.

options.title: Defer to scheduler redesign
options.body: Keep this as a Telegram-specific tracker until maintainers choose a shared ingress/dispatcher scheduling contract covering Telegram and related channels.

recommendation.title: Bridge busy lanes into collect
recommendation.body: Implement a Telegram-aware admission path that lets later same-lane ordinary updates reach active followup/collect while preserving control lanes, ack durability, and replay safety.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing candidate from current blame and repeated queue/reply admission history, and the decision crosses Telegram drain and core reply queue boundaries.
